# codex-0.165.0 verification

Status: Qualified anchor with bounded local-only store inspection.

Six compatibility cells passed on Codex 0.165.0 with gpt-6-astra on 2026-10-29; exec streaming remains the intentional skip ("not token-granular"). The question probe passed. Synthetic turns and later-process HERON-CODEX-420 recall passed. Exec emits no compaction signal. No native compaction failure was observed in the successful qualifying run, and no failure outcome was forced. The npm source remains @openai/codex.

## Probe settings

- Automatic compaction was exercised with `model_auto_compact_token_limit=20000`, a config override the probe set for its own turns. Lowered thresholds are a probe setting, not an HCN default.
- The executable under test was the task-isolated 0.165.0 install, with only that bin first on PATH for the probes. The globally installed codex stayed at 0.162.1 and was not upgraded. `version-source.snapshot.json` records the isolated install.
- The model catalog and the four app-server request schemas came from protocol metadata calls against the same isolated executable: `model/list` with and without `includeHidden`, and `codex app-server generate-json-schema --experimental`. No turn was started, no model inference ran and no auth probe was made.

## Replacement installation and store-observation limits

The rollout holds 2 `item_completed/ContextCompaction` events (lines 33 and 57) and 2 `compacted` rows with nonempty `replacement_history` arrays (8 and 9 items), window numbers 1 and 2, window links and `latest_token_usage_record` present.

On 0.165.0 the `compacted` rows nest their content under `payload` (`replacement_history`, `replacement_history_metadata`, `retained_context`, `window_id`/`previous_window_id`/`first_window_id`, `compaction_response_id`, `latest_token_usage_record`, `resume_metadata`); the row-level fields are `timestamp`/`ordinal`/`type` only. The 0.163.0 snapshot's extractor read row-level fields, so the two generations are not the same schema and each keeps its own assertions.

The store read was bounded and structural, over this probe's own synthetic rollout only. Large rows were truncated: the complete replacement contents were not inspected. Only derived structural metadata is included, not raw protected stores or encrypted content.

Lowered thresholds do not establish full-capacity handling or lossless recall. A smoke pass alone does not prove native replacement-history installation.

## What this anchor does not establish

- Native model acceptance was not re-probed on 0.165.0; the model catalog is the native roster, and the effort ladders come from the catalog's own `supportedReasoningEfforts`.
- The 0.165.0 catalog adds `gpt-6.1-terra` to the picker-visible roster. HCN's curated vocabulary has not gained it in this change, so this anchor records the native roster without demanding that it equal the curated list.
- No native compaction failure was observed and none was forced.

## Captured evidence

`seven.snapshot.json` and `questions.snapshot.json` are the smoke-suite receipts. `version-source.snapshot.json` records the published npm version observation. Fresh, question and later-recall NDJSON files contain selected native identity/assistant/result records, preserved byte for byte. Configuration-bearing hook and user frames are omitted; these are excerpts, not complete native streams. Other native fixture fields are unchanged.

The four app-server request schemas were generated by this CLI, not hand-edited. Native model/list captures cover visible models and includeHidden results.

The live probes use synthetic data only. Old versioned fixtures remain intact.
